Using mapped writes
column2: it's technically possible to expose stale

column1: post-eof data on a truncate up operation. Consider the following
example:
$ xfs_io -fc ""pwrite 0 2k"" -c ""mmap 0 4k"" -c ""mwrite 2k 2k"" \
-c ""truncate 8k"" -c ""pread -v 2k 16"" <file>
This shows that the post-eof data written via mwrite lands within
EOF after a truncate up. While this is deliberate of the test case
behavior is somewhat unpredictable because writeback does post-eof
zeroing
column2: and writeback can occur at any time in the background. For

column1: example
column2: an fsync inserted between the mwrite and truncate causes

column1: the subsequent read to instead return zeroes. This basically means
that there is a race window in this situation between any subsequent
extending operation and writeback that dictates whether post-eof
data is exposed to the file or zeroed.
To prevent this problem
column2: perform partial block zeroing as part of

column1: the various inode size extending operations that are susceptible to
it. For truncate extension
column2: zero around the original eof similar to

column1: how truncate down does partial zeroing of the new eof. For extension
via writes and fallocate related operations
range of the file to cover any partial zeroing that must occur at
the original and new eof blocks.
